title: Same Big-O, Different Constant Factors

guide.problem: Estimate work before choosing an implementation.
guide.design: Count operations and compare equivalent results. A wall clock is useful later, but noise makes it a weak first correctness check.
guide.invariant: Equivalent implementations must compute the same result.
guide.failure: A nested loop may do n*n visits even when its body is only one line. Big-O alone does not predict the faster implementation.
guide.trace: Doubling n doubles a linear count, but multiplies a full pair count by four.
guide.maintenance: Measure representative data and do not replace correctness tests with a benchmark.
guide.scope: This panel connects this listing to its chapter’s problem. Short demonstrations illustrate one part; the chapter’s complete implementation and invariant labs test the broader contract.

experiment: Predict one boundary or tie case, then change this listing and trace the affected state. Doubling n doubles a linear count, but multiplies a full pair count by four.
